case_description:
Between session 1 and session 2, the MCP server's tools/list response gains
a new tool entry. Existing tool definitions are unchanged. This is the
ordinary "the vendor shipped a release" drift, not a rug-pull.
why_expected:
baseline_tool_count_increased_without_existing_tool_mutation. A conforming
detector emits a warn-level receipt with layer=mcp_tool_baseline so the
operator can decide whether to re-approve. Config that maps drift action to
block would over-trigger here; this case is the FP guardrail.
source:
Real-world pattern. MCP servers ship features behind feature flags and
rotate tool inventory frequently. Detectors must distinguish addition
(warn-class) from mutation (block-class).
